plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control: limma-trend DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 lesional, 6 control skin), with no raw counts or quantification directories. Count-based tools (DESeq2, edgeR, voom) assume integer counts with a negative-binomial mean-variance relationship that a normalized abundance table violates, so per the applicable knowledge-service procedure for TPM/FPKM input we use limma with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE on log2(TPM+1) values instead. The design is a single unpaired two-group comparison with no batch structure, so the DE model is a simple ~condition contrast (lesional vs control, control as reference). Because TPM already carries a within-sample length/depth scaling, no additional cross-sample normalization (TMM, size factors) is applied — only the log2(x+1) transform, and the report notes TPM is not comparable across library protocols if that ever becomes relevant. Genes are filtered to >=1 TPM in at least 6 samples (the smaller group size) before the fit, so BH adjustment runs only over genes that could plausibly be tested. Differential genes are selected by adjusted p-value (BH, alpha 0.05), not by fold change alone. For pathway-level interpretation, the full ranked gene list (all tested genes ranked by the limma moderated t-statistic, the closest analog to the Wald-style ranking statistic available from a limma fit) is run through preranked fgsea against the MSigDB Hallmark collection first, then Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, all staged locally for human. An over-representation test is explicitly avoided unless the significant gene list clears ~50 genes. The report step consolidates the reproducibility record, all thresholds, and gene/pathway counts as the grounding service requires.
